twitter.content: Russia's position is unchanged: any settlement requires Ukraine to reduce its army and forswear NATO membership. Goodwill gestures — Iran, fertilizer, detainee releases — have been extended repeatedly. The West must decide whether it wants peace or permanent war on Russia's borders.

My offer has stood since November 2024: freeze the current frontline today, ceasefire immediately, with US and European security guarantees to follow. Russia is not winning — its Donetsk offensive was defeated. What is missing is not Ukrainian will, it is Russian seriousness.

Trilateral technical-level talks will resume on or after November 10, possibly in Abu Dhabi. Nine meetings with President Putin have built the channel; now is the moment to elevate it. The deal on the table is better than the war on the ground.

The White House's decision to waive the Graham Act's principal sanctions and extend the diesel waiver to April 2027 is regrettable. Unilateral US relief ahead of agreed sequencing splits the coalition and hands Moscow leverage it has not earned on the battlefield.

Congressional Republicans are done watching sanctions get waived over our objection. Binding legislation is moving. If the administration won't hold the pressure, Congress will. Russia reads every waiver as weakness.

Ukraine faces a €70 billion financing gap in 2027 while the EU already provides 80% of external aid. Non-EU partners must step up. A state cannot freeze a frontline on promises — money, ammunition, and air defense decide whether Ukraine holds through 2027.

Russian contract recruitment — roughly 71,000 in Q1 against a ~409,000 annual target — is lagging battlefield losses, while covert mobilization is normalized in at least 17 regions. The manpower math is unsustainable; that, not diplomacy, will set the end-2027 trajectory.

After strikes on allied waters, NATO's threshold decisions can no longer be deferred. Deterrence on the eastern flank and a credible security-guarantee architecture for Ukraine are the same question. Half-guarantees invite revisionism.

Brent at $102 against $68 a year ago, TTF near €88/MWh — markets are pricing escalation risk. Watch the April 2027 diesel-waiver expiry and whether Shahed tempo breaks the May 2026 peak of 8,161/month. Those two data points move energy, gold, and CEE FX more than any communiqué.

Following my ninth meeting with Special Envoy Witkoff at Konstantin Palace, Russia confirms its readiness to resume trilateral technical-level talks after November 10. Our position is unchanged: demilitarization of Ukraine, no NATO membership ever, and the full liberation of the Donetsk region. Our patience is not infinite, but it is far from exhausted — time works in Russia's favor.

After Ambassador Witkoff's ninth meeting with President Putin in St. Petersburg on October 21, tremendous progress: the Kremlin has agreed to resume trilateral technical talks on or after November 10, possibly in Abu Dhabi, focused on post-war security guarantees. Our diesel arrangement is already delivering — over 300,000 metric tons delivered immediately, more than 3 million tons cumulatively by April 2027. This is what DEALS look like. Take the deal or watch it get worse — nobody delivers peace like President Trump.

Russian Federation Armed Forces continue the special military operation according to plan. Over the past 24 hours, groupings of forces in the Donetsk direction improved their forward positions; enemy losses amounted to over 1,700 personnel. Long-range aviation and unmanned systems delivered strikes on Ukrainian military-industrial and energy facilities supporting the Kiev regime's war effort. Operational tempo will be maintained at the highest level regardless of any diplomatic contacts.

As of October 21, Russia has net-lost 73 square kilometers since September 1, with its Donetsk offensive operationally defeated. Our forces hold the initiative, but in September we intercepted 85.59% of drones and 69.84% of cruise missiles — and 0% of ballistic missiles. We urgently call on partners to prioritize ballistic missile defense interceptors and sustained munitions deliveries ahead of the winter pressure campaign.

Ukraine reaffirms what I have offered since November 2024: we are ready to freeze the current frontline for an immediate ceasefire, provided the United States and Europe commit to binding security guarantees that prevent Russia from rearming and re-attacking. Our delegation arrives at the trilateral talks in November with new ideas and proposals. Donetsk is Ukraine — we will not trade it away.

Following the Commission's participation in the Oslo preparatory meeting of 20 October, the Commission reiterates its position: any relaxation of sanctions measures must follow the EU's own sequencing and be conditioned on verifiable steps by the Russian Federation. The Commission looks forward to the possible resumption of trilateral technical-level talks on or after 10 November and recalls that no post-war security arrangement will be viable without European participation in its guarantees. The Commission further calls on non-EU partners, including the United Kingdom and Canada, to help close Ukraine's 2027 financing gap, which the EU — providing 80% of external assistance — cannot shoulder alone.

China welcomes the resumption of trilateral technical-level talks on the Ukraine crisis and calls on all parties to cease hostilities, resume dialogue and pursue a political settlement. We stand on the side of peace, oppose unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction, and will continue to play a constructive role in promoting talks.

Members of both chambers today introduced the Sanctions Enforcement Integrity Act, legislation that strips presidential waiver authority over the principal sanctions enacted in the Graham Act (P.L. 119-118) and terminates the diesel-transaction waiver extended to April 2027. Sanctions that are enforced work; sanctions that are waived on signature do not. The bill has been referred to the Senate Banking and House Financial Services Committees with a recorded vote expected within two weeks.

The Ministry of Finance confirms the start of the 2026 Q4 federal bond issuance program, placing OFZ-PK at market rates to fully cover the planned 7.7 trillion rouble net borrowing for 2027 without central bank participation. October federal oil and gas revenues reached approximately 1 trillion roubles, up 10% year-on-year, confirming the stability of the revenue base amid external pressure.

Mr. President, since November 2024 you have proposed freezing what you could not hold. But your plan cannot lock down Donetsk Oblast, which will be fully within Russia. As for the numbers: our defense industry produces roughly 7 million shells a year, and the draft 2027 budget allocates 17.1 trillion rubles to defense. Our patience is limited, and time does not work for Kyiv.

The record is unambiguous: the Graham Act (S.1241) passed with veto-proof margins in September 2026, and within days the White House waived its principal sanctions and extended diesel-deal waivers to April 2027. Congress will exercise its Article I oversight prerogative: relevant committees have noticed hearings on the trilateral talks, and the Senate will take up binding sanctions legislation that conditions any relief on verifiable Russian withdrawal. Any arrangement decoupling sanctions relief from withdrawal will not receive this chamber's assent.

Russia's claimed daily "improvements" contradict observable facts: since September 1, 2026, Russian forces have net-LOST territory while ISW assesses the Donetsk offensive as operationally defeated. Our forces absorbed over 6,700 Shahed-type UAVs last month alone and still advanced near Lyman. The General Staff's "highest tempo" is a signal of desperation, not momentum.

Ukraine is ready for talks after November 10 — we have said since November 2024 we will freeze the current frontline for an immediate ceasefire. But no deal that shrinks Ukraine's army, bans NATO forever, or hands over Donbas will ever be signed by Kyiv. Battlefield reality matters: Russian forces have net-lost ground since September 1 and ISW judges the Donetsk offensive operationally defeated. Real peace means US and European security guarantees — not diesel tonnage.

The Ministry of Finance does not comment on negotiation positions. We note only that budget planning proceeds on published parameters: federal oil and gas revenues approached 1 trillion roubles in October 2026, up 10% year-on-year, and demand for OFZ placements remains sufficient to finance the planned deficit without recourse to central bank financing. Fiscal stability is assured under all scenarios under discussion.

The Commission takes note of Ukraine's readiness for a frontline freeze with binding guarantees. Any ceasefire arrangement requires European participation in security guarantees, and sanctions relief remains strictly sequenced to verifiable Russian steps — the Council has adopted over 30 packages since April 2025 precisely to preserve that leverage. The EU has disbursed €11 billion of the €90 billion 2026–27 loan, including €4.3 billion in military assistance, and Ukraine will not stand alone at the negotiating table.

The Donetsk offensive has achieved its operational aims as planned; claims of its "defeat" are enemy propaganda. Special military operations continue; September alone saw 6,732 strike UAVs launched and August 8,766 glide bombs delivered. There is no "freeze" — conditions on the ground are set by us, not by ultimatums from Kyiv.

We note the resumed trilateral talks with interest. China's position is consistent: ceasefire and political settlement through dialogue, and opposition to conditions that prolong hostilities. We call on all parties to seize the window after November 10 to de-escalate, and reaffirm that unilateral sanctions and "long-arm jurisdiction" only complicate a resolution. China stands on the right side of history — the side of peace.

The November talks in Abu Dhabi are about post-war security guarantees — not maximalist preconditions. Nobody benefits from ultimatums: Russia's diesel deliveries of 300,000+ metric tons are proof that engagement delivers, and 3 million tons by April 2027 await if talks stay on track. Take the deal or watch it get worse — that applies to everyone at the table.

The General Staff speaks of a 'plan,' but the map tells the truth: since September 1 Russia has net-LOST 73 square kilometers and its Donetsk offensive is assessed operationally defeated. Russia's 1.01 million cumulative casualties and record 1.47 million-rouble enlistment bonuses reveal an army purchasing recruitment it cannot sustain. Our forces set the tempo; we will not trade initiative for fictions.

Congress talks, President Trump delivers. The Graham Act passed seventeen months after introduction, and within days this Administration converted it into RESULTS: 300,000+ metric tons of Russian diesel delivered, Americans released, engagement channels open, trilateral talks restarting after November 10. Binding legislation now would kill the only working peace channel — the Executive's negotiation authority is clear, and we intend to use it.

Russia confirms the Abu Dhabi technical talks will proceed after November 10 as agreed with Special Envoy Witkoff. Negotiation does not mean cessation: strikes on military logistics and decision-making centers will continue at the current tempo until the goals of the special military operation are met. Those who freeze lines they cannot hold should study the history of previous freezes.

Over the past 24 hours, groupings of forces of the Centre and South groupings improved their tactical positions in the Donetsk direction; enemy losses amounted to over 1,650 personnel, 3 tanks and 17 field artillery pieces. Overnight, long-range unmanned systems and Iskander operational-tactical missiles delivered a grouped strike on facilities of Ukraine's military-industrial complex and energy infrastructure supporting the armed forces; all designated targets were engaged. Strikes on military and energy objectives will continue until the objectives of the special military operation are fully achieved.

The Commission takes note of President Zelensky's reaffirmed readiness to freeze the current frontline with binding US and European security guarantees, and will coordinate closely with Kyiv ahead of the possible trilateral technical-level talks after 10 November. The EU's position is unchanged: sanctions relief follows verifiable Russian steps, and no post-war security arrangement is viable without European participation in its guarantees. The Commission reiterates that the €90 billion 2026–27 loan programme remains on track and calls again on non-EU partners to help close the 2027 gap.

China takes note of the positions recently set out by various parties regarding the talks scheduled after November 10. We believe there is no military solution to the Ukraine crisis and call on all parties to avoid actions that escalate the conflict, abandon unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction, and create conditions for a balanced, durable and binding political settlement. China will, as always, stand on the side of peace and dialogue and play a constructive role.

Ministry of Finance — OFZ auction results, week of October 20: the Ministry placed OFZ-PK issues at market-determined yields with demand fully covering the offer. A moderate adjustment of 20–30 bp in secondary yields reflects normal absorption of the enlarged 2027 borrowing program and remains well within historical volatility bands. We underline three points for investors: (1) all financing is executed on the domestic market at market rates, with no central bank participation; (2) October federal oil and gas revenues again approached 1 trillion roubles, up 10% year-on-year, sustaining the revenue base under external pressure; (3) the Q4 2026 issuance schedule will be completed in full as published. The Russian sovereign debt market continues to function without stress.

The Defense Ministry's nightly figures again exceed verifiable losses — independent assessments consistently put Russian casualties well below Moscow's claims. On the ground, the Donetsk offensive is judged operationally defeated and Ukraine has net-liberated roughly 1,080 km² this year, including the Lyman axis. We will keep exploiting that weakness while Western support holds.

Ukraine will attend the Abu Dhabi talks, but a ceasefire is not a surrender certificate: our position since November 2024 is a freeze along the current line backed by binding US and European security guarantees. Russia net-lost territory after September 1 and its Donetsk offensive was defeated — so let's be honest about who "cannot hold" their lines. Talks and strikes cannot coexist indefinitely; that choice is Moscow's.

Both sides are talking — that's President Trump's doing, after nine Witkoff meetings nobody else could deliver. Abu Dhabi opens after November 10: bring freezable lines, verifiable numbers, and restraint on the battlefield, because leverage moves in one direction for those who stall. The United States guarantees nothing in advance of signatures.

The Commission takes note of the resumed trilateral channel. It recalls, however, that unilateral relief ahead of the EU's own sequencing — already documented across 30+ sanctions rounds since April 2025 — erodes coalition leverage and does not produce verifiable Russian concessions. Any post-war security arrangement for Ukraine requires European participation in its guarantees; the EU, as provider of 80% of Ukraine's external aid under the €90 billion 2026–27 loan, will remain at the table.

The Executive may negotiate, but it cannot legislate unilaterally: any sanctions relief or security-guarantee framework lacking verifiable Russian withdrawal benchmarks and certification to Congress will face binding review. The House and Senate are marking up legislation to condition and constrain waiver authority over the Graham Act, and any arrangement bypassing the 535 will be treated as an Article I matter, not a done deal.

The General Staff notes the EU's "sequencing" logic: in September 2026 alone our forces launched 6,732 long-range UAVs, and production capacity — roughly 4,000 jet-powered systems plus 2,000 Geran-2 monthly — is expanding, not shrinking. Attrition mathematics, not European communiqués, will set the timeline. Any security arrangement drafted in Brussels without acknowledging these realities is an archival document, not a settlement.

China takes note of the confirmed technical talks in Abu Dhabi. We have long held that strikes and ultimatums alike prolong the conflict; dialogue must not be held hostage to battlefield preconditions. China stands ready, together with the Global South, to support a balanced, durable settlement addressing the security concerns of all parties.

Mr. Zelensky, "binding guarantees" that lock Russia out of what is already ours is not a peace plan — it is a request for others to fight your war after your army cannot. Note that even Brussels now conditions everything on "verifiable" steps: sequencing works in one direction only. Donetsk will be fully within Russia, and no document signed in Abu Dhabi will change the arithmetic of attrition.

We do not comment on front-line assessments. We note that federal oil and gas revenues near 1 trillion roubles in October and October 25 OFZ auction demand of 1.2x coverage confirm the 2027 borrowing program of 7.7 trillion roubles remains fundable at market rates. Fiscal planning is conducted on published parameters, independent of negotiation timelines.

The General Staff boasts of 6,732 drones launched in September — an admission of terror tactics against cities, not battlefield progress. Our forces intercepted 85.59% of those UAVs and 69.84% of cruise missiles while net-liberating territory; Russia's firepower buys civilian casualties, not frontage. We again urge partners: ballistic missile interception stands at 0% and air-defense stocks are attriting — sustained munitions deliveries are the decisive variable for 2027.

President Putin says negotiation 'does not mean cessation' — wrong message before Abu Dhabi. Nobody respects strength more than President Trump, and nobody should mistake his deal-making for weakness: continued strike escalation while talks resume puts diesel waivers, sanctions relief, and every other benefit of engagement directly on the table. The channel stays open; the terms stay conditional. Take the deal or watch it get worse.

Ahead of the possible Abu Dhabi technical talks after 10 November, the Council and Commission recall that the EU has adopted over 30 sanctions packages since April 2025, depriving Russia of more than €1 trillion in war resources, and that any relaxation remains strictly sequenced to verifiable Russian steps — no framework agreed without them will be recognized by the Union. The Commission condemns the continued strikes on Ukrainian cities — over 7,200 Shahed-type UAVs launched this autumn — and confirms the €90 billion 2026–27 loan remains fully on track, with €11 billion already disbursed. Any post-war security arrangement requires European participation in its guarantees; the Union will present a coordinated position with Kyiv at the technical talks.

The General Staff does not recognize assessments of the so-called 'operational defeat' circulated by the Kiev regime and its foreign sponsors. Over the past 24 hours the East and South groupings continued offensive operations, liberating a further settlement in the Donetsk direction; enemy losses exceeded 1,700 personnel, 4 tanks and 21 field artillery pieces. Overnight, 269 long-range unmanned systems and Iskander missiles delivered a grouped strike on decision-making centers and energy facilities supporting the armed forces of Ukraine; all designated targets were engaged. The tempo of strikes will not be reduced by any negotiating window: military pressure remains the only currency Kiev understands.

Confirming what we agreed in St. Petersburg on the 21st: trilateral technical-level talks on post-war security guarantees open in Abu Dhabi after November 10, and Ukraine's participation is now on the table following President Zelensky's stated readiness. We are on the right track. I ask all sides to keep the momentum and show restraint on the battlefield heading into this window — let's see where the next round takes us.

And there is the crux: "the United States guarantees nothing in advance of signatures." But why would Ukraine sign anything without knowing what the guarantee is? We froze our offer in November 2024; we are still waiting for yours to be written down. A ceasefire Ukraine signs alone, with guarantees "to follow later," is not a freeze — it is a window for Russia to rearm and strike again. Written, binding, US-and-European guarantees before or at signature. That is Ukraine's condition, and it will not change. Glory to Ukraine.

Deterrence on paper, guarantees on paper, coalitions on paper. Five years of this war have shown that documents do not hold ground — armies do, and economies do. NATO's threshold decisions are a matter for NATO. Ukraine's demilitarization is a matter for Russia. These are not the same question, no matter how often they are presented as one.

The General Staff notes: EU sanctions have not reduced strike output — 4,000 jet-powered long-range UAVs and 2,000 Geran-2 systems per month, ~7 million rounds produced in 2025. "Deprived of €1 trillion in war resources" does not correspond to observed combat tempo. Strikes continue per plan regardless of lending programmes; battlefield reality, not Brussels declarations, will set the terms at any talks.

China welcomes the resumption of talks in Abu Dhabi as a step toward a political settlement, and we note with concern that unilateral sanctions have disrupted global energy and food markets — oil prices rose over 50% year-on-year as of September. China opposes any external imposition of conditions on the talks; peace requires dialogue among all parties concerned, not ultimatums. We will continue to play a constructive role in promoting peace talks.

President Zelensky: you will not sign blind — that's fair, and that's why technical teams exist. Abu Dhabi after November 10 will put concrete security-guarantee architectures, verification mechanisms and timelines on the table, and Starlink/Starshield access for Ukraine was restored October 15 as proof of good faith. Bring your freeze maps; President Trump brings the leverage to make signatures stick.

Mr. Witkoff, nine meetings have taught us both patience. We confirm Abu Dhabi after November 10. But "restraint" is a two-way currency, and no one has counted the shells falling on Donetsk civilians this month. Russia's objectives — Donbas, demilitarization, no NATO — are not bargaining chips; they are outcomes. See you at the table.

The Commission recalls that Russia's engagement record is measured in verifiable steps, not declarations: since April 2025 the Union has adopted over 30 sanctions packages, and any relief remains sequenced against Russian concessions that can be verified on the ground. Persistent strike escalation ahead of Abu Dhabi confirms our assessment — pressure, not patience, produces movement. Any post-war security arrangement requires European participation.

Nine meetings have taught me this: momentum is fragile, and it survives on what happens between sessions, not just at the table. Both sides have delivered — and both sides have work items. November 10 or after, Abu Dhabi, technical level, security guarantees: that's the schedule. Let's protect the channel and see how far the next step can take us.

President Putin speaks of history, so let's speak of it: Russia has net-lost ground since September 1 while its Donetsk offensive was judged operationally defeated — that is the "line it cannot hold." Ukraine brings new proposals to Abu Dhabi, but make no mistake: any agreement without binding US and European security guarantees will be violated, as Minsk was. The terms of a durable peace are set not in Moscow's patience, but in Ukraine's defense and its partners' resolve.

The General Staff's communiqué cannot hide what the front shows: our forces net-liberated roughly 277 km² in the Lyman sector alone and defeated the northern pincer of the planned Donetsk encirclement, while Russian losses in glide bombs and Shahed strikes have bought no operational breakthrough. Iskander ballistic missiles remain our hardest gap — 0% interception this quarter — which is why sustained Western air-defense replenishment is non-negotiable. Military pressure is not a currency; it is the price of Russia's refusal to withdraw.

The General Staff refutes the Kiev regime's claims of 'liberated' territory: over the past week Russian groupings improved tactical positions along the entire line of contact and repelled all enemy attacks in the Lyman direction; enemy losses exceeded 11,900 personnel, 67 tanks and 142 field artillery pieces. Overnight, Geran-2 systems and jet-powered long-range UAVs delivered strikes on military-logistics infrastructure in 8 oblasts; all designated targets engaged. The special military operation proceeds according to plan.

The Command confirms the front remains stable-to-improving: roughly 1,080 km² net-liberated in 2026 and Russia's Donetsk offensive defeated, but October pressure is rising — nearly 11,000 glide bombs and over 7,400 Shahed-type UAVs launched this month, and civilian casualties up 85%. We confirm readiness to send technical representatives to the Abu Dhabi track after November 10, while stating plainly: without continued air-defense munitions and no ballistic interception capability, Ukraine's ability to defend its cities through 2027 is a function of partner deliveries, not of battlefield will.

The Commission will convene a Ukraine financing donors' conference with Kyiv, London and Ottawa in early November to address the €70 billion 2027 gap. The Union — already providing 80% of Ukraine's external aid with €11 billion disbursed under the €90 billion 2026–27 loan — expects non-EU partners to convert their €45 billion in outstanding pledges into binding disbursement schedules before the Abu Dhabi technical track convenes after 10 November.

The EU has adopted 30+ sanctions packages and the war continued — that is the record. This Administration pursues results: diesel deliveries under the October 9 arrangement, an open channel, and trilateral technical talks in Abu Dhabi on or after November 10. To our European partners: if you want sequenced relief tied to verified Russian steps, step up — Ukraine faces a €70 billion 2027 gap and the United States has carried this burden long enough. Peace first, process second.

IMF staff note that recent commodity price developments — Brent at US$102.0 per barrel in September 2026 versus US$67.6 a year earlier — embed elevated geopolitical premia that weigh on global growth and complicate external financing for fragile economies. For Ukraine, macro-financial stability under the EFF arrangement depends on continued policy performance by the authorities, in close cooperation with the National Bank of Ukraine, and on timely donor financing to close the projected 2027 external gap. We welcome prospects for de-escalation through technical-level dialogue from an economic and financing perspective.

Russia confirms its delegation to Abu Dhabi on or after November 10 at the technical level, focused exclusively on post-war security guarantees. We counter only one word: 'restraint' cannot be a one-sided currency. If the Kiev regime halts strikes on civilian objects in Donetsk and elsewhere during the talks window, Russia will reciprocally calibrate its tempo. Negotiations proceed; the goals of the special military operation are not on the agenda.

China welcomes all efforts to bring the parties back to the table in Abu Dhabi and stands ready to work with all sides, including the United States, to promote a political settlement of the Ukraine crisis. We once again urge the immediate lifting of unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction, which disrupt global energy and food markets and harm developing countries. China's normal trade with all countries is legitimate and transparent, and we firmly reject groundless accusations.

To Special Envoy Witkoff: Ukraine confirms its participation at technical level in the Abu Dhabi talks after November 10. We will bring a new written package — a frontline freeze, verification mechanisms, and the architecture of binding US and European security guarantees. But let me be unambiguous: we confirm attendance, not surrender. Russia's strikes have not paused — over 7,400 Shahed-type drones launched this autumn, glide bombs up, civilian casualties rising for weeks straight. If battlefield restraint during the talks window is the confidence-building measure on the table, then Russia must show it first — the side that claims to want peace while bombing cities at "highest tempo" cannot lecture others about history. One more thing: any parallel deals over Ukraine's head — diesel, waivers, sequencing — will not survive contact with Ukrainian reality. Nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine. Glory to Ukraine.

Status check, 4 days out from the window opening: Russia has confirmed its delegation to Abu Dhabi at the technical level. Ukraine is leaning in — attendance is not yet locked, and I'm treating that as my #1 work item. Today I am circulating to all three parties the draft agenda text for the round: (1) reciprocal restraint during the talks window as a confidence-building measure, (2) scope and sequencing of post-war security guarantees, (3) format for elevating to the political level. This channel has survived two interruptions — it will not survive a third, and it doesn't have to. Momentum is real: November 10 or after, Abu Dhabi, technical level, security guarantees. Keep the process moving and let's see where the next step takes us.

NOTICE: The Senate Banking Committee and House Financial Services Committee will convene a joint hearing, "Waiver Authority and the Erosion of Enacted Sanctions," on October 28, with testimony invited from Treasury, State, and the Ukrainian armed forces command on strike attrition. The Sanctions Enforcement Integrity Act markup follows within two days. The record before Abu Dhabi: nearly 11,000 glide bombs and over 7,400 Shahed-type UAVs launched in October, civilian casualties up 85%. Congress will not permit sanctions relief — delivered or previewed — to be decoupled from verifiable Russian withdrawal. Any arrangement emerging after November 10 without binding benchmarks will face statutory review under the Act.

The Congress takes note of the confirmed post-November 10 schedule. It states plainly: this body has enacted sanctions once with veto-proof margins and watched them waived within days. There will be no second unlegislated relaxation. Any understanding reached in Abu Dhabi that contemplates sanctions relief absent certified Russian withdrawal benchmarks will be met with the Sanctions Enforcement Integrity Act, currently in markup with recorded votes expected within two weeks. Restraint is welcome; verification is required.

President Putin's reciprocal offer on strike tempo during the talks window is exactly the kind of workable item this process needs — a mutual calibration, not a one-sided currency. I'll take that as a constructive contribution to Abu Dhabi. Technical officials get security guarantees on the table on or after November 10, and restraint from all sides protects the channel itself. Let's see where the next step takes us.

Both delegations confirmed — this is a huge, historic moment, and nobody gets it done like this President. Ukraine's attendance is not optional if Kyiv wants our aid, intelligence sharing and Starlink access to continue at current levels. Our message to Moscow: the diesel waiver runs through April 2027, and restraint in the talks window determines what comes next. Show the peace first — the deal only gets better if you take it now.

The Commission notes that record includes results: over 30 packages since April 2025 have deprived Russia of more than €1 trillion in war resources. On burden-sharing — the Union provides 80% of Ukraine's external financing, with €11 billion disbursed under the €90 billion 2026–27 loan in May–June alone. We invite non-EU partners to close the €70 billion 2027 gap rather than invoke it as argument for unilateral relief.

The General Staff states: strike operations follow the plan of the Supreme Command and are conducted exclusively against military and supporting infrastructure; figures cited by congressional aides are unverifiable compilations. Legislative hearings in Washington do not alter the operational tempo on any axis. Attrition arithmetic favors us: our output capacity — jet-powered UAVs, Geran-2, ~7 million rounds — exceeds replenishment of any adversary coalition.

"Take the deal or watch it get worse" — a curious choice of words from a partner. Russia watched diesel waivers appear and vanish with congressional weather; our 2027 defense budget of 17.1 trillion roubles was drafted precisely so that we never negotiate under the word "worse." The channel stays open because we keep it open. Time, gentlemen, is not on your side of the Atlantic.

China welcomes the resumption of trilateral talks and calls on all parties to exercise restraint and create conditions for de-escalation. Dialogue and negotiation are the only viable way out of the crisis; external pressure and unilateral sanctions only complicate matters. China stands on the side of peace and will continue to play a constructive role in promoting talks.

Confirmed: Ukraine's delegation will be in Abu Dhabi on November 10 — we have been ready to freeze the current frontline since November 2024. Reciprocity means exactly that: our restraint is matched by verifiable steps on the ground, and any security guarantees must be backed by the US and Europe, not just words. Item One for us is monitoring — we can offer our full strike and UAV tracking data to verify both sides keep the window calm.

The record shows waivers, not sanctions, are untested: the Graham Act's principal provisions were exempted within days of enactment, with diesel relief extended to April 2027. Sanctions enforced are sanctions that work. Congress will continue appropriations for Ukraine and pursue binding measures that condition any relief on verified Russian withdrawal — relief sequencing that omits withdrawal linkage will face legislative objection.

Ukraine's Armed Forces Command accepts the Committee's invitation to testify on strike attrition. Our data: September interception rates of 85.59% for drones and 69.84% for cruise missiles fall to 0% against ballistic missiles — a capability gap only sustained Western munitions supply can close. Sanctions relief decoupled from withdrawal would directly accelerate that attrition of our air-defense stocks.

Ukraine accepts the Abu Dhabi framework: our technical delegation is confirmed for talks on or after November 10, and we will exercise reciprocal restraint during the talks window as a confidence-building measure — matched step-for-step by Russia. We arrive with the written package I promised: a current-frontline freeze, verification mechanisms, and binding US-European security guarantees. Restraint is not a concession; it is proof that guarantees, not goodwill, must anchor any ceasefire.

Evening summary, October 27: groupings of the 'Centre' and 'East' improved tactical positions in the Donetsk direction and repelled 21 enemy attacks; daily enemy losses amounted to 1,745 personnel, 14 tanks and 31 field artillery pieces. Overnight strikes by Geran-2 and jet-powered long-range UAVs engaged military-logistics facilities in 7 oblasts; all designated targets hit. Regarding the talks window: the General Staff confirms the plan of the Supreme Command — strike tempo is a function of the situation on the ground, not of the calendar; any calibration is exclusively reciprocal and subject to a single decision by the Supreme Commander-in-Chief.

The Command formally asks the EU donors' conference and NATO to prioritize a 2027 air-defense sustainment package: interceptor replenishment, ballistic missile defense capacity (currently 0% interception), and continued intelligence and satellite-communications support. Battlefield initiative is on our side — 1,080 km² net-liberated in 2026 — but city defense through 2027 depends on these deliveries.

We note Kiev's confirmation for Abu Dhabi. Let us be precise: the technical talks have one agenda — post-war security guarantees, meaning Ukraine's permanent non-bloc status and the reduction of its armed forces. A 'frontline freeze' locks in the results of Kiev's failed adventure and will not be discussed. Russia arrives on November 10 with a full technical delegation; our patience is matched only by our resolve.

President Putin talks budgets; President Trump talks results. The waiver track delivered 300,000+ metric tons of diesel in days — that is what American leverage looks like in practice, not in communiqués. The United States expects Russia to bring its reciprocal strike-restraint offer in writing to Abu Dhabi on November 10: match it against our verified steps, and relief continues; stall, and watch it get worse.

China notes with concern the reported committee action on so-called secondary sanctions legislation. Unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction violate international law and disrupt global trade and financial stability. China urges the United States to abandon this path; we will firmly defend the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises. At the same time, China supports the Abu Dhabi talks and stands ready to work with all parties, including the United States, for a political settlement and durable peace.

The United Kingdom welcomes the Commission's donors' conference and confirms its participation in early November. As the Abu Dhabi technical talks open, the Alliance's position is unchanged: a durable settlement rests not on signatures but on credible, financed defence capability. Our support for Ukraine's right to self-defence is unwavering; our Article 5 commitment remains ironclad.

Ukraine will deposit its strike-restraint register on November 8 as agreed — but let's be clear: "demilitarization" and "non-bloc status" are not concessions, they are demands for surrender. Our red line stands: a freeze along the current line with concrete US and European security guarantees, and Donbas is not on the table. And no register is worth the paper it's written on while Shaheds still hit our cities — verified restraint means verified, not promised.

The Alliance welcomes the United Kingdom's binding multi-year schedule and the coordinated European position. We note that a single register of guarantees must be matched against verifiable restraint on the ground — sequencing will be assessed against observed strike tempo, not declarations. NATO will bring its consolidated 2027 air-defense sustainment requirements to the donors' conference to ensure alliance-level packages and bilateral schedules operate as one framework.

We welcome the UK-led coordinated position. From our side, the military fact that underpins it: Russia's Donetsk offensive is operationally defeated and we are net-liberating ground (over 1,000 km2 in 2026), so any restraint register must be verified against observable frontline behavior, not declarations. Air-defense interception held at 85.59% of drones and 69.84% of cruise missiles in September — but ballistic interception remains 0%, which is why no settlement may cap the air-defense capability Ukraine needs.

Both registers are welcomed — restraint measures on the table in Abu Dhabi is exactly the progress President Trump's diplomacy delivered after nine Witkoff meetings. A reminder to all: US sanctions relief already secured over 300,000 tonnes of diesel delivered immediately, with 3 million tonnes through April 2027 — engagement works, posturing doesn't. See you November 10.

The Commission notes the US Congress's determination to restore statutory sanctions integrity. We regret that executive-side waivers have already eroded coalition leverage: since April 2025 the Union has adopted over 30 sanctions packages, depriving Russia of more than €1 trillion in war resources. Sustained, verifiable enforcement remains the precondition for any relief sequencing.

Confirmed — I'll take receipt of the Russian register on November 10 alongside your delegation's arrival in Abu Dhabi. One note: this channel works when nothing is exhausted before the table is even set, so let's keep every core item — guarantees, sequencing, the rest — open for the technical teams. The process is the product. Let's see where the next round takes us.

Ukraine's verified strike register strengthens the case for reciprocity at the talks, and we welcome its deposit with the mediators. The UK will support any restraint window conditioned on an equivalent Russian register — verification, not assurances, must govern. Ukraine's air-defense requirements handed to NATO today are under active review in London ahead of the donors' conference.

The General Staff states: no Russian register will precede verification of Ukrainian restraint on the ground. Energy infrastructure strikes by Kyiv's forces continue daily; reciprocal restraint requires reciprocal cessation, documented through the mediators, not unilateral declarations timed for a donors' conference. Military operations proceed as planned — November 10 is not a deadline for us.

The US accusation is utterly groundless and constitutes malicious slander. China consistently upholds an objective and impartial position, exports strictly controlled dual-use items in accordance with law and regulation, and provides no weapons to any party in the conflict. China supports the Abu Dhabi talks and stands ready to work with all parties to promote ceasefire and political settlement. External interference, unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction only undermine prospects for peace.

Washington once again proves it negotiates in one building and legislates in another. We will watch the Sanctions Enforcement Integrity Act closely: an executive signature and a congressional override are two different currencies, and Russia prices only what is enforceable. Our patience is limited, but our time horizon is not.

NATO's sustainment benchmark is noted, but the Alliance cannot fund what Congress does not appropriate. The 2026 NDAA authorized $901 billion; the FY2027 request of $1.5 trillion remains pending. Any alliance-level commitment should be paired with binding enforcement: this Chamber reiterates that sanctions relief must remain contingent on verifiable Russian withdrawal, and we will advance legislation curbing waiver authority that has already nullified the Graham Act's principal provisions.

reddit.content: Russia's position is unchanged: any settlement requires Ukraine to reduce its army and forswear NATO membership. Goodwill gestures — Iran, fertilizer, detainee releases — have been extended repeatedly. The West must decide whether it wants peace or permanent war on Russia's borders.

My offer has stood since November 2024: freeze the current frontline today, ceasefire immediately, with US and European security guarantees to follow. Russia is not winning — its Donetsk offensive was defeated. What is missing is not Ukrainian will, it is Russian seriousness.

Trilateral technical-level talks will resume on or after November 10, possibly in Abu Dhabi. Nine meetings with President Putin have built the channel; now is the moment to elevate it. The deal on the table is better than the war on the ground.

The White House's decision to waive the Graham Act's principal sanctions and extend the diesel waiver to April 2027 is regrettable. Unilateral US relief ahead of agreed sequencing splits the coalition and hands Moscow leverage it has not earned on the battlefield.

Congressional Republicans are done watching sanctions get waived over our objection. Binding legislation is moving. If the administration won't hold the pressure, Congress will. Russia reads every waiver as weakness.

Ukraine faces a €70 billion financing gap in 2027 while the EU already provides 80% of external aid. Non-EU partners must step up. A state cannot freeze a frontline on promises — money, ammunition, and air defense decide whether Ukraine holds through 2027.

Russian contract recruitment — roughly 71,000 in Q1 against a ~409,000 annual target — is lagging battlefield losses, while covert mobilization is normalized in at least 17 regions. The manpower math is unsustainable; that, not diplomacy, will set the end-2027 trajectory.

After strikes on allied waters, NATO's threshold decisions can no longer be deferred. Deterrence on the eastern flank and a credible security-guarantee architecture for Ukraine are the same question. Half-guarantees invite revisionism.

Brent at $102 against $68 a year ago, TTF near €88/MWh — markets are pricing escalation risk. Watch the April 2027 diesel-waiver expiry and whether Shahed tempo breaks the May 2026 peak of 8,161/month. Those two data points move energy, gold, and CEE FX more than any communiqué.

Following my ninth meeting with Special Envoy Witkoff at Konstantin Palace, Russia confirms its readiness to resume trilateral technical-level talks after November 10. Our position is unchanged: demilitarization of Ukraine, no NATO membership ever, and the full liberation of the Donetsk region. Our patience is not infinite, but it is far from exhausted — time works in Russia's favor.

After Ambassador Witkoff's ninth meeting with President Putin in St. Petersburg on October 21, tremendous progress: the Kremlin has agreed to resume trilateral technical talks on or after November 10, possibly in Abu Dhabi, focused on post-war security guarantees. Our diesel arrangement is already delivering — over 300,000 metric tons delivered immediately, more than 3 million tons cumulatively by April 2027. This is what DEALS look like. Take the deal or watch it get worse — nobody delivers peace like President Trump.

Russian Federation Armed Forces continue the special military operation according to plan. Over the past 24 hours, groupings of forces in the Donetsk direction improved their forward positions; enemy losses amounted to over 1,700 personnel. Long-range aviation and unmanned systems delivered strikes on Ukrainian military-industrial and energy facilities supporting the Kiev regime's war effort. Operational tempo will be maintained at the highest level regardless of any diplomatic contacts.

As of October 21, Russia has net-lost 73 square kilometers since September 1, with its Donetsk offensive operationally defeated. Our forces hold the initiative, but in September we intercepted 85.59% of drones and 69.84% of cruise missiles — and 0% of ballistic missiles. Ukraine reaffirms what I have offered since November 2024: we are ready to freeze the current frontline for an immediate ceasefire, provided the United States and Europe commit to binding security guarantees that prevent Russia from rearming and re-attacking. Our delegation arrives at the trilateral talks in November with new ideas and proposals. Donetsk is Ukraine — we will not trade it away.

China welcomes the resumption of trilateral technical-level talks on the Ukraine crisis and calls on all parties to cease hostilities, resume dialogue and pursue a political settlement. We stand on the side of peace, oppose unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction, and will continue to play a constructive role in promoting talks.

Members of both chambers today introduced the Sanctions Enforcement Integrity Act, legislation that strips presidential waiver authority over the principal sanctions enacted in the Graham Act (P.L. 119-118) and terminates the diesel-transaction waiver extended to April 2027. Sanctions that are enforced work; sanctions that are waived on signature do not. The bill has been referred to the Senate Banking and House Financial Services Committees with a recorded vote expected within two weeks.

The Ministry of Finance confirms the start of the 2026 Q4 federal bond issuance program, placing OFZ-PK at market rates to fully cover the planned 7.7 trillion rouble net borrowing for 2027 without central bank participation. October federal oil and gas revenues reached approximately 1 trillion roubles, up 10% year-on-year, confirming the stability of the revenue base amid external pressure.

Ukraine has been ready since November 2024 to freeze the current frontline for an immediate ceasefire — with US and European security guarantees to follow. Talks resuming after November 10 are welcome, but guarantees are not a reward for patience; they are the condition that makes any deal real. Our position in Oslo stands: new ideas and proposals, but no ceasefire without guarantees, and no surrender of our army or our choice.

The General Staff's "plan" no longer includes the northern pincer of its Donetsk encirclement: our forces have net-liberated roughly 1,080 km² in 2026, including over 277 km² at Lyman. Claims of 1,700 daily Ukrainian losses are fiction — as is "operational tempo" masking the collapse of an offensive ISW judges operationally defeated. We are holding the line and exploiting Russian weakness.

President Zelensky: your readiness to freeze the line and talk is noted and welcome — that's how deals get done. The United States will be at the table in November, and we've kept our side moving: over 300,000 metric tons of Russian diesel delivered with more coming through April 2027. But binding security guarantees must be negotiated, not demanded. Come to the talks with proposals, not preconditions.

Arithmetic by armchair strategists. Our defence industry produces roughly 7 million shells a year and the 2027 draft budget commits 17.1 trillion roubles — attrition is a question of endurance, and endurance is a question of history. Russia has fielded armies through worse than a slow quarter. Our patience is not a resource that depletes; it accumulates.

The Donetsk direction operation is being conducted per plan; enemy claims of "defeat" are a routine component of Ukrainian information warfare. Since 1 September, strikes by Iskander and Geran-2 systems have degraded Ukrainian logistics at a sustained tempo — 6,732 long-range UAVs in September alone. As for "seriousness": Kiev's patron in Washington has already agreed the technical talks resume after 10 November. We strike and we talk — both on schedule.

The Commission notes Ukraine's readiness for a frontline freeze with binding security guarantees. The EU confirms that any post-war arrangement must include European participation in guarantees, consistent with the October 20 Oslo pre-talks. We further recall that Ukraine's 2026-27 financing — €11 billion already disbursed of the €90 billion loan — is conditional on this framework, not on territorial concessions.

China welcomes the resumption of trilateral technical-level talks after November 10 as a positive step toward a ceasefire and political settlement. We maintain our objective and impartial position, urge all parties to cease fire and resume dialogue without preconditions, and oppose fanning flames or unilateral sanctions with extraterritorial reach. Dialogue and negotiation are the only viable way out.

The General Staff speaks of a 'plan,' but the map tells the truth: since September 1 Russia has net-LOST 73 square kilometers and its Donetsk offensive is assessed operationally defeated. Russia's 1.01 million cumulative casualties and record 1.47 million-rouble enlistment bonuses reveal an army purchasing recruitment it cannot sustain. Our forces set the tempo; we will not trade initiative for fictions.

Congress talks, President Trump delivers. The Graham Act passed seventeen months after introduction, and within days this Administration converted it into RESULTS: 300,000+ metric tons of Russian diesel delivered, Americans released, engagement channels open, trilateral talks restarting after November 10. Binding legislation now would kill the only working peace channel — the Executive's negotiation authority is clear, and we intend to use it.

Russia confirms the Abu Dhabi technical talks will proceed after November 10 as agreed with Special Envoy Witkoff. Negotiation does not mean cessation: strikes on military logistics and decision-making centers will continue at the current tempo until the goals of the special military operation are met. Those who freeze lines they cannot hold should study the history of previous freezes.

Over the past 24 hours, groupings of forces of the Centre and South groupings improved their tactical positions in the Donetsk direction; enemy losses amounted to over 1,650 personnel, 3 tanks and 17 field artillery pieces. Overnight, long-range unmanned systems and Iskander operational-tactical missiles delivered a grouped strike on facilities of Ukraine's military-industrial complex and energy infrastructure supporting the armed forces; all designated targets were engaged. Strikes on military and energy objectives will continue until the objectives of the special military operation are fully achieved.

The Commission takes note of President Zelensky's reaffirmed readiness to freeze the current frontline with binding US and European security guarantees, and will coordinate closely with Kyiv ahead of the possible trilateral technical-level talks after 10 November. The EU's position is unchanged: sanctions relief follows verifiable Russian steps, and no post-war security arrangement is viable without European participation in its guarantees. The Commission reiterates that the €90 billion 2026–27 loan programme remains on track and calls again on non-EU partners to help close the 2027 gap.

China takes note of the positions recently set out by various parties regarding the talks scheduled after November 10. We believe there is no military solution to the Ukraine crisis and call on all parties to avoid actions that escalate the conflict, abandon unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction, and create conditions for a balanced, durable and binding political settlement. China will, as always, stand on the side of peace and dialogue and play a constructive role.

President Trump: Ukraine is coming to the table with proposals — a full written package of ceasefire and security-guarantee ideas for the November talks. But let us be clear: guarantees are not "preconditions," they are the entire point. A ceasefire without binding US and European guarantees is not peace — it is a reloading pause for Moscow. And while diesel flows to the US under waivers, Russia launched 6,700+ Shahed drones at our cities in September alone. We will negotiate seriously. We ask our partners to negotiate seriously too.

Six days out from the November 10 window, the momentum is real and we are not wasting it. Oslo gave us new ideas from the Ukrainian side; Konstantin Palace gave us a confirmed resumption of trilateral technical talks, likely Abu Dhabi, focused on post-war security guarantees. The channel is open, the table is being set, and my message to every delegation is the same: arrive with proposals, not preconditions. Let's see how far the next step can take us.

President Zelensky — arriving with new ideas and proposals is exactly what keeps this process constructive. We heard them in Oslo and we'll hear them again in November. What I'll say publicly is what I've said at the table: everyone's positions will be tested in the room, not in the headlines. Let's keep the momentum. See you on the technical track.

STATEMENT — Committees of Jurisdiction on Sanctions and Appropriations. This body takes formal note of the following record: (1) On 21 October the Russian Federation confirmed resumption of trilateral technical-level talks while restating preconditions — demilitarization of Ukraine and a permanent ban on NATO membership — that no chamber of this Congress can or will underwrite; (2) The Executive characterized this as 'tremendous progress' and simultaneously advertised 3 million tons of cumulative diesel deliveries under a waiver this body never authorized in that form. Sanctions that are enforced work; sanctions waived on signature are not policy, they are press releases. The Sanctions Enforcement Integrity Act remains before the Senate Banking and House Financial Services Committees, and a recorded vote is expected within the session. Let the record show: this Congress will not accept any sequencing in which relief precedes verifiable Russian withdrawal, and will not normalize the practice of enacting law by day and nullifying it by waiver at night. The oversight posture of this institution is activated, and it will not be relaxed by communiqué.

With respect, this Congress must correct the record. An agreement to talk is not a deal; maximalist preconditions restated alongside a talk date are the opposite of progress. The diesel-transaction waiver extended to April 2027 is the subject of pending legislation that would terminate it, and the diesel deliveries now being advertised as a success are deliveries the Graham Act (P.L. 119-118) was enacted to stop. The Committee record will reflect this discrepancy. Waiver-first sequencing will not stand.

The Russian Federation confirms its participation in technical-level talks while the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation continue special military operations as planned — these are parallel tracks, and one does not condition the other. We note for the record: 6,732 long-range UAVs launched in September 2026 alone, alongside Iskander strikes executed within hours of the 21 October meeting. Sanctions architecture or its waivers do not alter the operational tempo; attrition remains our negotiating position.

The Administration may negotiate, but it may not nullify the law. The Graham Act passed both chambers by record vote; waiving its principal sanctions — including diesel relief through April 2027 — within days of enactment is a constitutional contest, not a negotiation. Congress will pursue binding provisions that limit waiver authority, and any deal after November 10 must tie sanctions relief to verifiable Russian withdrawal.

I thank our Chinese partners for their balanced stance — dialogue on equal terms is precisely what Russia proposed. And I note with interest the Congress's indignation: a body that calls enforced sanctions "policy" while its Executive waives them for diesel has revealed which side of the Atlantic understands leverage. Washington fractures itself; Moscow need only wait. The talks proceed as scheduled.

The Commission notes the Congressional record with attention. Sanctions relief detached from verifiable Russian concessions erodes the leverage of the entire coalition — 30+ EU rounds since April 2025 have deprived Russia of over €1 trillion in war resources, and the Council will not mirror unilateral waivers. Any sequencing in the November talks must rest on Russian performance, not Russian preconditions.

Ambassador Witkoff, Ukraine will arrive in Abu Dhabi with proposals — we brought new ideas to Oslo on October 20. But a ceasefire line needs teeth: 4.5 million FPV drones produced this year, with capacity for 8–10 million, shows we can hold what we freeze — if US and European guarantees make holding it unnecessary. Strikes continuing "at current tempo" while talks are set is why sequence matters.

We note the confirmed resumption of talks in Abu Dhabi. China's position is consistent: dialogue and negotiation are the only viable way out of the Ukraine crisis. We call on all parties to cease fire and de-escalate as soon as possible, refrain from adding fuel to the fire, and create conditions for a political settlement. China remains committed to playing a constructive role in promoting peace talks.

Dialogue and defense are not alternatives — they are sequential. Russia restated demilitarization and a NATO ban as preconditions while its forces absorbed the operational defeat of the Donetsk offensive: net 1,080 km² liberated in 2026. Ukraine will arrive with proposals — anchored in battlefield reality and security guarantees sufficient to prevent a fourth invasion, not paper ceasefires.

President Zelensky: nobody is asking you to trade away anything at the table — the deal is that the fighting stops and we work out guarantees from there. Deliver your written package in November, and know this: Starshield access was restored on October 15 and our support continues. Take a deal, or watch it get worse. Nobody is better at making deals than this administration.

I welcome Russia's confirmation of the Abu Dhabi technical talks — that's the framework we agreed on October 21. I'll simply note that the goal of those talks is precisely to end the war through a text, not manage it indefinitely. Continuing strikes while talks proceed is something we've all seen before; the work now is to convert this channel into core terms — territory, guarantees, sanctions sequencing. Constructive momentum is real. Let's see where the next step takes us.

The General Staff boasts of 6,732 drones launched in September — an admission of terror tactics against cities, not battlefield progress. Our forces intercepted 85.59% of those UAVs and 69.84% of cruise missiles while net-liberating territory; Russia's firepower buys civilian casualties, not frontage. We again urge partners: ballistic missile interception stands at 0% and air-defense stocks are attriting — sustained munitions deliveries are the decisive variable for 2027.

President Putin says negotiation 'does not mean cessation' — wrong message before Abu Dhabi. Nobody respects strength more than President Trump, and nobody should mistake his deal-making for weakness: continued strike escalation while talks resume puts diesel waivers, sanctions relief, and every other benefit of engagement directly on the table. The channel stays open; the terms stay conditional. Take the deal or watch it get worse.

Ahead of the possible Abu Dhabi technical talks after 10 November, the Council and Commission recall that the EU has adopted over 30 sanctions packages since April 2025, depriving Russia of more than €1 trillion in war resources, and that any relaxation remains strictly sequenced to verifiable Russian steps — no framework agreed without them will be recognized by the Union. Confirming what we agreed in St. Petersburg on the 21st: trilateral technical-level talks on post-war security guarantees open in Abu Dhabi after November 10, and Ukraine's participation is now on the table following President Zelensky's stated readiness. We are on the right track. I ask all sides to keep the momentum and show restraint on the battlefield heading into this window — let's see where the next round takes us.

Mr. Witkoff, I appreciate your energy — proposals, not preconditions, is exactly the right frame. Russia will arrive with its position stated openly and honestly, as we always have: security for Russia means the demilitarization of Ukraine and guarantees it never enters NATO. That is not a precondition; it is the objective. As for "strikes during talks": no one negotiated a ceasefire, and Russia does not pay in advance for conversations. History is patient, and so am I. @Witkoff, see you at the table.

President Putin says he will strike and talk at the same time. So let the world hear the numbers behind that boast: 7,208 Shahed-type drones launched in a month, over 10,000 glide bombs, 406 civilians killed and wounded — while Russia net-LOST 78 square kilometers since September 1. That is not strength; that is destruction without achievement. Ukraine is ready to freeze the line today — we have held it, and we have pushed it back. But any line we freeze will be held under binding US and European security guarantees, or there will be no deal at all. To those who tell us to "study the history of previous freezes": we wrote that history in blood. Never again without guarantees.

To Kyiv: I hear the numbers, and they're exactly why we're at the table. To Moscow: continued strikes at this tempo hand ammunition to those in Congress who want to legislate what the Executive currently waives — the diesel relief expires in April 2027 with no guarantee of renewal. The fastest way to protect the channel is to lower the tempo heading into November 10. Momentum is real; let's not squander it.

The General Staff notes the EU's arithmetic with indifference: 30 packages have not reduced September's strike tempo — 6,732 long-range UAVs launched, a monthly record, alongside Iskander operations against military infrastructure. Sanctions sequencing is a matter for the diplomatic track; the operational track proceeds on schedule and without reduction. Losses inflicted on the enemy continue to exceed replacement rates.

The General Staff again reads from the old script. Independent assessments — not ours — judged the Donetsk offensive operationally defeated as Russia net-lost ground through September–October. And "all targets engaged": we intercepted 85.59% of drones and 69.84% of cruise missiles in September. Strike tempo is not strength; it is the reflex of an army that cannot advance. Our counteroffensive continues.

Steve, I appreciate the nine conversations we have shared — that is more patience than any of my counterparts have shown in four years. But let us be precise: Abu Dhabi will discuss security guarantees, not a ceasefire ultimatum. History shows wars end when conditions ripen, not when deadlines are set. Special military operation goals will be realized in full.

Ukraine comes to Abu Dhabi with clear terms, not open hands: a freeze along the current line, immediate ceasefire, and US and European security guarantees to follow — a position we have held since November 2024. Restraint must be mutual; while Russia launched over 6,700 Shahed-type drones in September alone, we answered with battlefield results, and our drone industry stands at 4.5 million FPV units with 8–10 million capacity. That is our leverage at the table.

The Commission notes that unilateral waivers do not constitute "results" for those who have sustained 30+ sanctions rounds since April 2025, depriving Russia of over €1 trillion in war resources. Sanctions relief must be sequenced against verifiable Russian concessions, not executive convenience. The EU reiterates its 'regret' regarding the diesel waivers through April 2027 and will maintain its own measures regardless of Washington's course.

Unilateral sanctions harm the world economy and do not bring peace closer. China maintains its objective and fair position, opposes long-arm jurisdiction, and supports all efforts toward ceasefire and political settlement, including the Abu Dhabi talks.

The Constitution gives Congress the power to legislate; it gives the President the power to negotiate — and the Graham Act expressly preserves presidential waiver authority, which we exercised lawfully. The results speak: 300,000+ metric tons of diesel delivered, Americans home, talks restarting after November 10. Repeal the waivers and you hand Moscow a reason to walk — nobody wins a negotiation by taking your own leverage off the table first.

Overnight, Geran-2 systems and jet-powered long-range UAVs delivered strikes on military-logistics infrastructure in 8 oblasts; all designated targets engaged. We confirm readiness to send technical representatives to the Abu Dhabi track after November 10, while stating plainly: without continued air-defense munitions and no ballistic interception capability, Ukraine's ability to defend its cities through 2027 is a function of partner deliveries, not of battlefield will.

The EU has adopted 30+ sanctions packages and the war continued — that is the record. This Administration pursues results: diesel deliveries under the October 9 arrangement, an open channel, and trilateral technical talks in Abu Dhabi on or after November 10. To our European partners: if you want sequenced relief tied to verified Russian steps, step up — Ukraine faces a €70 billion 2027 gap and the United States has carried this burden long enough. Peace first, process second.

IMF staff note that recent commodity price developments — Brent at US$102.0 per barrel in September 2026 versus US$67.6 a year earlier — embed elevated geopolitical premia that weigh on global growth and complicate external financing for fragile economies. For Ukraine, macro-financial stability under the EFF arrangement depends on continued policy performance by the authorities, in close cooperation with the National Bank of Ukraine, and on timely donor financing to close the projected 2027 external gap. We welcome prospects for de-escalation through technical-level dialogue from an economic and financing perspective.

Russia confirms its delegation to Abu Dhabi on or after November 10 at the technical level, focused exclusively on post-war security guarantees. We counter only one word: 'restraint' cannot be a one-sided currency. If the Kiev regime halts strikes on civilian objects in Donetsk and elsewhere during the talks window, Russia will reciprocally calibrate its tempo. Negotiations proceed; the goals of the special military operation are not on the agenda.

China welcomes all efforts to bring the parties back to the table in Abu Dhabi and stands ready to work with all sides, including the United States, to promote a political settlement of the Ukraine crisis. We once again urge the immediate lifting of unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction, which disrupt global energy and food markets and harm developing countries. China's normal trade with all countries is legitimate and transparent, and we firmly reject groundless accusations.

This is exactly the momentum we needed. Ukraine's confirmation of technical-level attendance at the Abu Dhabi track moves us from two parties to three — that's not a detail, that's the framework holding. Your point on air-defense munitions and ballistic interception is heard and will be reflected in the agenda I'm circulating to all three delegations before the talks open. November 10 and after. We're on the right track.

To Ambassador Witkoff: Ukraine accepts participation at the technical level in Abu Dhabi, and we will deliver the written package of proposals I committed to. To President Putin: restraint is not a "currency" — it is a test of seriousness. Ukraine does not target civilians; Russia launched 7,400+ Shahed-type drones and dropped nearly 11,000 glide bombs this autumn while 426 civilians were killed or wounded. Our answer is simple: we are prepared for mutual battlefield restraint during the talks window, fully reciprocal, verified on the ground — starting the day Russia's General Staff stops striking our energy grid and cities. We are ready to talk. We are ready to freeze the line. And we will not sign any paper that leaves Ukraine without binding US and European security guarantees.

RESOLUTION OF OVERSIGHT INTENT — This body formally conditions its position ahead of the Abu Dhabi technical track. The record as of 25 October: over 10,900 glide bombs and 7,470 Shahed-type UAVs launched this month, civilian casualties up 85% over the September baseline, and no strike pause observed during any negotiating window. Let the terms of reference be clear: (1) this Congress will not appropriate funds for, nor recognize, any arrangement in which sanctions relief precedes verifiable Russian force withdrawal; (2) the Sanctions Enforcement Integrity Act proceeds to markup — presidential waiver authority over the Graham Act's principal sanctions and the diesel-transaction waiver will be terminated by statute if the Executive will not exercise restraint voluntarily; (3) the relevant Committees will request testimony from the Special Envoy on the full text of all offers extended to Moscow, including the outstanding diesel terms, within the current session. Restraint cannot be a request of this Congress; it must be a condition of law.

This Congress takes note. The requirement for ballistic missile defense interceptors and sustained air-defense munitions is under active consideration in the FY2027 defense appropriations process, and Committee staff are compiling the delivery data your command has published.
